name: Canopy folk
one_line: They went up and never came down: platforms lashed in the crotches of the giants, vine bridges between them, and a fire that sits in a box of clay because the whole village is made of wood.

needs: an old-growth stand with three or more giants (stand.json giant) within 60 m: the trees are the village
no ladder is lowered for a stranger: the player climbs the trunk and the branch graph to the first platform (§AU); their own rope ladders come down once the headman has met you
water in the crown (bromeliad tanks, tree holes, rain off a bark gutter into a bamboo cup) and a stream at the foot for the rest

staples: fruit and nuts off the crown: fig, wild mango and durian, or hazel, chestnut, acorn and beech mast, by biome
birds' eggs from the nests the bridges pass
squirrel, bird and monkey by blowpipe and snare on the branch roads
tree-fern crozier, epiphyte shoots and sap boiled down in season
how: the crown read like a field: which tree fruits this month, which hollow hums, which nest is within reach
a vine loop round trunk and waist, footholds cut in the bark, the loop whipped up as you go
blowpipe and snare along the branches; the dart's poison milked from the upas tree
the hive smoked with a bundle of embers and a third of the comb left
no canopy garden is attested anywhere, so none here: the crown is foraged, and the only thing planted is the fig for a bridge
preserve: nuts and dried fruit in bark boxes hung from the rafters, out of the damp and the rats
meat and fish from the foot smoked on a rack over the hearth box
honey in a bamboo tube stoppered with leaf

fuel.note: everything burned is carried up: dead branch and bark stripped from the giants themselves, bamboo and frond hauled from the foot in a net; no log ever comes up, too heavy for a rope and too long-burning for a box; the woodpile is a bundle hung under the eaves and it is always small, which is the whole of their restraint

shelter.form: a platform lashed in the crotch of a giant 8–15 m up, four to ten props under it, a leaf roof and a floor of bark or split bamboo; one family to a tree; the trees joined by vine bridges so the village is a web with no ground floor

TEMPERATE_RAINFOREST.fuel: dead hemlock and cedar branch off the giants, brush hauled up in a net; fir pitch stands in for dammar
TEMPERATE_RAINFOREST.food: hazelnut, salal and huckleberry off the crown edge; eggs; squirrel and grouse; salmon carried up from the foot in season
TEMPERATE_RAINFOREST.shelter: cedar-bark shingles on a plank floor, moss stuffed in the lashings against the wet
TEMPERATE_RAINFOREST.palette: cedar red, moss green, fog, lichen grey

TROPICAL_RAINFOREST.fuel: dead branch, palm frond, dry bamboo from the foot
TROPICAL_RAINFOREST.food: figs, wild mango and brazil nut off the crown; honey; monkey and toucan by blowpipe; bromeliad water
TROPICAL_RAINFOREST.shelter: a platform on a strangler-fig buttress, palm thatch, split-bamboo floor
TROPICAL_RAINFOREST.palette: buttress grey, fig green, bromeliad red, honey gold

JUNGLE.fuel: bamboo above all, hauled up and split; frond in the wet
JUNGLE.food: durian, rambutan and wild mango in season; squirrel and hornbill by blowpipe; sago pith carried up from the foot
JUNGLE.shelter: bamboo floor and walls, rattan lashing, leaf thatch, the Papuan way
JUNGLE.palette: bamboo yellow, rattan brown, monsoon grey, hornbill black and white

CLOUD_FOREST.fuel: damp branch dried in a net over the hearth box; bamboo
CLOUD_FOREST.food: wild avocado and the laurels' fruit, tree-fern crozier, eggs; water from every bromeliad tank and tree hole
CLOUD_FOREST.shelter: a low walled platform against the cold, moss-chinked, the hearth box inside
CLOUD_FOREST.palette: moss green, mist white, orchid pink, bromeliad red

TEMPERATE_DECIDUOUS.fuel: dead oak and beech branch, brush; a winter's bundles hung under every eave
TEMPERATE_DECIDUOUS.food: acorn, beech mast, chestnut and hazel off the crown; maple sap boiled down in spring; squirrel, pigeon and dormouse; the hive in the hollow oak
TEMPERATE_DECIDUOUS.shelter: oak-bark shingles on a walled platform against the winter; the bridges sag under snow and are re-lashed each spring
TEMPERATE_DECIDUOUS.palette: oak brown, bare-branch grey, mast gold, snow

knows: which fig ripens which month, and that the fig is the crown's bread
bromeliad tanks and tree holes as cups: which are sweet and which are frog soup
the hive tree by its hum and by the bees at the hole
strangler fig from rubber fig: the one you climb and the one you train
the upas tree's milk for the dart, and the tree-fern crozier that feeds
plantkeeper.teaches_flavour: why the crown is a field with no ground: fruit that never falls ripe, eggs, honey, a squirrel's cache; why the midden tree at the foot grows the fattest figs
plantkeeper.teaches_practical: tip the frogs out and drink the bromeliad tank; never take the whole clutch; smoke the hive and leave a third; the upas milk is for the dart, never the wound; a hearth box that has cracked is a burning village

wants_from_player: pitch and resin to seal a lashing

techniques.name: Reading the crown
techniques.verb: loop a vine round the trunk and your waist, cut footholds, whip the loop up as you climb; in the crown read the tree: which branch fruits, which hollow hums, which nest is within reach, which bromeliad tank is sweet; take part and come down slow
techniques.teaches: the headman's first lesson because it is what the climb is for: forage lifted off the floor into a field that never empties if you take part; Efe men climb twenty metres for honey on an ordinary day, and one Baka man in fifteen dies of the fall, so slow is the rule and the bridges only matter once you have a reason to be up there
techniques.unlocks: the player harvests fruit, eggs, comb and water in the crown of any giant tree; a giant reads as a larder

techniques.name: Vine bridge
techniques.verb: twist liana or hardy-kiwi vine into cables as thick as an arm, anchor them round two trunks, hang a floor of cross-poles and walk it in; rebuild it every third year, before it rots
techniques.teaches: a bridge that is a rope, not a beam: the whole village hangs between the trees on something that must be remade, so the remaking is the village's calendar; the Iya folk rebuild theirs every three years and the Q'eswachaka is rewoven every June, and the year it was not, it fell
techniques.unlocks: the player crosses their bridges; taught, lashes a short one between two close trees (a gap, not a gorge)

techniques.name: Rope ladder
techniques.verb: two bast ropes, bamboo rungs lashed a forearm apart, coiled at the platform lip and let down; hauled up at dusk
techniques.teaches: the village's door: down for their own, up for the dark and for strangers; a notched pole hung under a Papuan tree house shakes with every step and tells the house someone is coming
techniques.unlocks: once the headman has met you their ladders come down for you; the player can hang one from a platform or a thick branch

techniques.name: Living root bridge
techniques.verb: plant a rubber fig on each bank, lead its aerial roots across a hollowed palm trunk or a bamboo, twist them, tie them, wait: fifteen to thirty years before it bears a person, and it grows stronger every year after
techniques.teaches: the ultimate harmony technique: the one bridge that gets stronger as it ages and that nobody has to rebuild — a village planting a crossing its grandchildren will walk; the Khasi ones hold fifty people and are thought to last centuries
techniques.unlocks: the camp's crossing that never rots; the ruin's one signature that grows

techniques.name: Tree platform
techniques.verb: pick a giant with a crotch 8–15 m up, lash a frame of poles into it with rattan, prop it from below with four to ten poles, floor it with bark or split bamboo, roof it with leaf
techniques.teaches: a house with no ground: above the mosquitoes, the flood and the things that walk at night; it rots in a decade and is lashed again on the same scars, so the tree is the house and the platform is only its coat
techniques.unlocks: the camp's shelter: one family per giant, the village the size of the stand

techniques.name: Hearth box
techniques.verb: a box of poles floored with a hand of clay and a bed of sand, set on the platform; the fire lives in it and never touches the floor; if the clay cracks, the folk cut the box loose and let it fall
techniques.teaches: fire on wood is the whole tension of living up here: a spilt hearth is not a lost hut but a burning village and a burning tree, so the fire is kept small, watched and boxed — restraint made furniture
techniques.unlocks: the player lays a fire on a platform, a bridge-head or a big branch without burning it; the ember comes up in a bark bundle

techniques.name: Dammar torch
techniques.verb: knock the hardened resin off the bark where a dipterocarp has bled, pound it and pack it into a leaf or bark tube or a split bamboo, light it at the hearth box
techniques.teaches: the forest's own candle: slow, bright, sweet-smoking, and it drips less than pitch; hung at the bridge-head it lets a crossing be made after dark
techniques.unlocks: the dammar torch: a slow bright hand light in the wet forests; fir pitch is the temperate stand-in

gives: vine and rattan cable, rope ladders
wants: pitch and resin from the collier

ladder: fire in a box on the first platform; the ember carried up in bark
the crown read: fruit, eggs, comb — forage, but lifted
bark boxes of nuts and dried fruit under the eaves, honey in bamboo: storage
the bridge-weaver: the first who does not climb for food
cable, ladders and honey go down the ladder; salt, blades and pitch come up
growth.restraint: the woodpile is a bundle and the fire is a box, and both stay small because a village made of wood cannot afford otherwise; eggs by the one, never the clutch; the hive smoked and a third left; the strangler fig climbed, never felled; a bridge rebuilt every third year so no gap grows wider than a vine can be twisted; the root bridge planted for the grandchildren
growth.ceiling_hint: one family per giant: three giants are a hamlet, ten are the tribal ceiling; their ladders stay up for a stranger and come down once the headman has met you; a tropical crown with figs and hives grows fastest, an oak crown feeds a winter on mast, a cloud forest stays a few platforms in the mist

signatures.what: a ring of giants with old lashing scars girdling the trunks at a height, and footholds cut or worn into the bark up to the first crotch; nothing on the ground at all
signatures.restore: cleared: a new platform lashed on the old scars, the footholds re-cut
signatures.inherits: the giants are chosen: the first platform goes up in days, not seasons

signatures.what: a rotted vine line lying across a gap, bridge-poles in the litter under it, half of it still hanging from one trunk
signatures.restore: restored: a new bridge on the old anchor trees
signatures.inherits: the anchors and the line of the bridge

signatures.what: a living root bridge across the stream at the foot, thicker and stronger than the day its makers died: the one thing here that grew after them
signatures.restore: restored as it stands: it never needed restoring; the camp keeps it clear of strangler and rot
signatures.inherits: a crossing from day one, and a village that reads as old

signatures.what: a mound of nutshell, eggshell, bone and old comb at the foot of the biggest tree, dropped from above for a century; figs and fruit trees thick on it
signatures.restore: cleared: the new camp's midden falls on the old one
signatures.inherits: the midden's fruit trees, and the proof the crown fed people

signatures.what: notched poles rotting against the trunks and a hung trunk-ladder gone to punk; the notches read as a way up
signatures.restore: restored: new notched poles hung on the old pegs
signatures.inherits: the way up for folk who cannot climb bark

ruin.plants_differ: figs and fruit trees thick on the midden at the foot of the biggest tree, where the wild stand would be mixed; rubber figs along the stream with their roots knotted across it; epiphytes stripped thin on the village trees and heavy on the trees around; nothing else, because a canopy village leaves the ground alone

aesthetic.silhouette: platforms in the crotches of giants under leaf roofs, bridges sagging between them, ladders coiled at the lip; smoke leaking from a box; nothing on the ground but a midden
sounds: the slap of a vine loop on a trunk
props: bark boxes hung under the eaves

real_world.region: southern lowlands of Papua, Indonesia — living peoples, about 4,000 Korowai and 5,600 Kombai
real_world.note: a family house sits about 8–12 m up (the Kombai guoro 3–15 m) in a banyan or on a tree pruned to a central post, four to ten props, sago-bark floor and walls, leaf roof, rattan lashing, a fireplace to each room; a notched dry trunk hung from the house is the ladder, and it shakes to announce a visitor; sago and bananas the staple, one sago palm a week per household. The 35 m house in the BBC's Human Planet (2011) was commissioned for the film crew, as the BBC admitted in 2018: houses of 40–50 m are for cameras and tourists, not daily life

real_world.analogue: Khasi and Jaintia living root bridges (jingkieng jri)
real_world.note: aerial roots of the rubber fig (Ficus elastica) led across a stream on hollowed areca trunks or bamboo and knotted; usable after ten to twenty-five years by different accounts, holding fifty people when mature and thought to last centuries; the Umshiang double-decker at Nongriat; about 75 geo-located in 2017; on UNESCO's tentative list since 2022; the Khasi also grow ladders and platforms of root

45 m long and 14 m above the river, five to six tonnes of hardy-kiwi vine (Actinidia arguta, shirakuchi-kazura — not wisteria), rebuilt every three years; legend has the Heike refugees building it to be cut behind them; a national Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property, with steel cable hidden in the vine today

real_world.region: Apurímac river, Cusco, Peru — living Quechua communities
real_world.note: the last Inca grass-rope bridge, about 28 m: four communities twist ichu grass family by family into cables and reweave the whole bridge in three days each June, on UNESCO's intangible heritage list since 2013; when the pandemic stopped the renewal in 2021 it fell, and was rebuilt — a bridge that is a rope is a bridge only as long as it is remade

real_world.analogue: Forest foragers who climb: Aka, Mbuti, Efe, Baka, Batek
real_world.region: Congo basin and peninsular Malaysia — living peoples
real_world.note: a vine looped round trunk and waist, footholds cut with an axe, the loop whipped up as they climb; the Batek build rattan 'vine ladders' at 45° to bridge canopy gaps and climb 50 m trees daily; Efe men climb 19 m on average for honey and up to 52 m; the Baka smoke the hive and leave three strips of comb 'so the bees can come back'; in one study 6.6% of Baka men's deaths were climbing falls

dammar, the resin that dipterocarps (Shorea, Hopea, Vatica) bleed and harden on the bark, was gathered from natural exudations as 'damar laut' and used locally for torches; Malaysia's forestry department still lists the resin torch as the traditional use of balau resin

hunter-gatherers famous for the silent blowpipe and poison dart; wild pig prized, deer, smaller game and fish; wild sago pith the staple, trampled and sun-dried; ferns and fruit gathered; most now settled but living from the forest
